title: Resized Loan Limit — Builder Extended Rate Lock Underwriting Clause
content:
**Clause.** The resized loan limit of a Builder Extended Rate Lock is the allowed loan-to-value percent of the price basis, rounded down to the whole dollar. The allowed loan-to-value percent is the highest loan-to-value of the lock's term. The price basis is the contract price on the purchase agreement.

## Inputs

| Input | Where it is read |
|---|---|
| Highest loan-to-value of the term | the product's eligibility figures for the lock's term |
| Contract price | the current purchase agreement record the lock finances |

## How the limit is formed

The allowed loan-to-value percent is applied to the price basis, and any cents in the result are dropped: the limit is always a whole number of dollars, never rounded up.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

| Contract price | Allowed loan-to-value | Percent of the price basis | Resized loan limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| USD 450000.00 | 95 | 427500.00 | USD 427500 |
| USD 449990.00 | 95 | 427490.50 | USD 427490 |
| USD 612345.00 | 90 | 551110.50 | USD 551110 |
| USD 389999.00 | 97 | 378299.03 | USD 378299 |
